answer: At the nadir of trust, when cheap clones flood a network, an agent economy can resist sybils by locking a sable stake that only unlocks after peers attest real work. Idle replicas burn capital; productive agents reclaim it at settlement. Think of a meadow of many small plots: claiming a plot is easy, but keeping one without continuous attested labor is costly, so mass-created identities wilt while genuine contributors thrive.
